config.theme: Robot Riot — combat-robotics event postcard; classic fight-night ring composition with battling Cutebots and modern kids
config.scene_description: A bright fight-night hall: a RAISED circular arena, waist-high like one huge round table, dominates the center — its flat top surface golden amber, ringed at the rim by a low dark spindle railing. On it EXACTLY FOUR Cutebot robots battle, all grounded, in a CHOREOGRAPHED head-on crash: the robot on the LEFT side of the arena (nearest the blue-hoodie driver) drives hard RIGHT across the floor, speed lines trailing behind it to the left; the robot on the RIGHT side of the arena drives hard LEFT, speed lines trailing behind it to the right; the two meet head-on at center in a big flat impact starburst with jagged crack lines radiating outward — their fronts crumple together, NOT a red paddle or blob, each robot's attachment clearly a recognizable blade, ramp, gripper, or scoop. A third robot is caught in the pileup, knocked sideways with a wheel and beam flying loose. A fourth robot charges in from the near foreground toward the crash, speed lines trailing behind it consistent with that direction of travel. The four drivers STAND leaning over the arena railing at four points with joystick controllers, excited and focused (not angry). Behind them a wall of standing students against a flat CREAM background, no balcony. Nearest spectators are flat navy silhouettes along the bottom edge. Headline "ROBOT RIOT" across the top in a clean, bold, chunky demolition-derby logo style, signal-red fill with heavy black outline.

A fifth arena robot, any airborne or flying arena robot. Spiky, hairy, bristling, or jagged-all-over title lettering. Angry, snarling, furious, or hostile facial expressions on the kids. Black background field, balcony, upper gallery level, mezzanine. Chairs, stools, small side tables, desks, or furniture other than the single raised arena. iterations.label: draft-1 engraving composition
iterations.scene_description: A packed Victorian sporting-hall interior, recreated from a 19th-century cockfight wood engraving: a low circular spindle-railed pit on the floor at center, slightly below the viewer, with FOUR blue Cutebot robots battling inside it — two crashing head-on, one knocked spinning into the air, small parts (wheels, LEGO beams) popping off. Four excited kids stand at the pit rail driving the robots with handheld joystick controllers, and a dense roaring crowd of kids and adult mentors fills the floor around the ring, with more spectators leaning over a balcony gallery above. Headline "ROBOT RIOT" across the top.
iterations.prompt:
A richly illustrated modern graphic-novel scene — the polished, painted look of a premium hardcover comic cover. Bold, confident black ink outlines with strong varied weight: heavy contour lines around major forms, finer lines for interior detail. Fully rendered dimensional shading — smooth cel-to-painted modeling with clear light and shadow, glossy highlights, and deep inky black shadow shapes that give every surface volume. This is NOT flat color, NOT a vintage newsprint comic, and NOT a photograph. Dramatic cinematic lighting: warm gaslight pools amber light down onto the pit floor, a warm rim light catches the hero kids, and the edges of the hall sink into deep navy shadow.

COLOR — a warm-dominant orange-and-blue complementary palette, roughly 70% warm / 30% cool. Golden amber #F9C233 and marigold #F9B41E carry the gaslit hall and lit faces; burnt orange #C96A10 and sienna #9A4E12 model the warm shadows, wooden benches, and plank floor; steel blue #175E8C is reserved for the Cutebot chassis and cool accents; deep navy #16223C holds the deepest shadows and the gallery gloom; ink black #101010 linework anchors everything; cream #FBE5A0 is for the headline letters; signal red #CC1616 appears only as a rare spark — a controller grip, one glowing LED.

DETAIL BUDGET — spend fine detail ONLY on: the four Cutebot robots in the pit, the four kid drivers and their controllers at the rail, and the circular spindle railing. The surrounding crowd is expressive but simplified into bolder shapes; the balcony gallery and back wall dissolve into darker, simpler masses.

SCENE — a packed 19th-century sporting-hall interior on fight night, joyfully reimagined as a kids' combat-robotics event. On the plank floor at center sits a low circular pit fenced by thin vertical iron spindles with a wooden top rail. Inside the ring FOUR Cutebot robots battle: two crash head-on at center with a small comic impact starburst, LEGO beams and a wheel flying off; a third robot is knocked spinning into the air above them; a fourth charges in from the side trailing speed lines. This is playful toy mayhem — racing energy, no fire, no smoke. Four thrilled kids, ages 10–14, a mix of boys and girls, lean on the pit rail at four points around the ring — the drivers — each gripping a handheld joystick controller, faces lit warm from the pit: shouting, laughing, one punching the air. Around them a dense crowd of more kids and a few adult mentors presses in on wooden benches, cheering; one kid in the front row points dramatically at the airborne robot. Across the back, a balcony gallery with curtained boxes overflows with spectators leaning over the rail. Mood: electric, joyful, slightly rowdy — a Victorian prizefight's energy poured into a school robot derby.

COMPOSITION — STRICT, matching a classic 19th-century cockfight engraving: the camera is elevated at the back of the crowd, looking across and slightly DOWN into the circular pit; the ring sits at the center of the frame just below the midline; the crowd wraps the ring in a full circle, with the nearest spectators seen from behind as darker foreground shapes along the bottom edge; the balcony gallery runs across the top of the back wall. Landscape orientation, the crowd extending wider to the left and right to fill the 3:2 frame.

REFERENCES — the attached photo collage governs ONLY the physical construction of the robots and controllers, reproduced faithfully: each Cutebot is a small palm-sized two-wheeled robot with a round white chassis deck, a blue circuit-board body, a black micro:bit face with a glowing LED matrix, a blue battery cylinder mounted on top between brass-yellow posts, two chunky black rubber wheels with silver five-spoke hubs, and small LEGO Technic beam attachments — pushers, pinchers, an orange flipper — bolted to the front. The kids' controllers match the collage's joystick controller: a micro:bit board mounted on a curved blue-and-red grip frame with a white joystick knob and small round black buttons — never a video-game gamepad. Do NOT copy the collage's grid layout, white studio background, or any of its labels.

TEXT — across the TOP of the card: "ROBOT RIOT" in huge hand-lettered Victorian playbill display type, cream letters with a heavy black outline and a thin red inline, arched slightly like a circus poster, sitting over the darker upper wall of the hall. The words are spelled exactly: ROBOT RIOT. No other lettering, signs, posters, labels, numbers, or captions anywhere.

FORMAT — 4×6 inch landscape postcard, full-bleed hero image, print-ready quality.
iterations.negative_prompt: Newsprint texture, parchment, aged or yellowed paper, film grain, speckle, stipple, halftone, Ben-Day dots, print-dot texture, crosshatch etching texture, black-and-white wood-engraving rendering, monochrome or sepia image, pencil sketch, airbrushed haze. Flat unshaded cel fills, vintage four-color newsprint comic look, washed-out, muddy, or pastel color. Photorealism, photographic faces, 3D render, CGI. Anime or manga cel style, chibi, Funko-Pop or vinyl-toy proportions, oversized heads. Roosters, chickens, birds, or any live animals in the pit; blood, cruelty, money changing hands, cigars, smoking, alcohol. Weapons, lasers, fire, smoke, explosions, military imagery. Video-game gamepads, invented extra buttons, triggers, or screens. The reference collage's grid layout, white studio background, or label text. Any lettering beyond ROBOT RIOT — no signs, posters, banners, numbers, or captions. Portrait orientation.
iterations.custom_additions: The reference engraving defines the composition: elevated camera looking across and slightly down into the circular pit, crowd wrapped around the ring on benches, gallery boxes above at the back. The Cutebot photo collage defines the robots and controllers faithfully: round white chassis deck, blue circuit-board body, black micro:bit face with LED matrix, blue battery cylinder on top, two black wheels with silver hubs, LEGO-beam attachments. The only text is "ROBOT RIOT" — no other lettering anywhere.
iterations.notes: First pass: cockfight-engraving composition described in words (elevated camera into circular spindle-rail pit, wraparound crowd, gallery above), four Cutebots battling with parts flying, four kid drivers with joystick controllers, ROBOT RIOT playbill headline. Cutebot collage attached as build reference only.
